title: Clear conditions
summary: Readable conditions: say each rule once, plainly, and use guard clauses instead of nesting. Delve decides what every step does.

steps.title: Say it once, say it plainly
body: Conditions grow clutter. A few rewrites are always safe, in any language:
| `if (x > 0) return true; else return false;` | `return x > 0;` |
A comparison already **is** a boolean. Wrapping it in `if ... return true else return false` adds four lines that say nothing.

steps.prompt: Match each cluttered condition to its plain form.
Which is equivalent to this function body for every input?

steps.title: Guard clauses
body: Nested ifs push the real work to the right and make you hold every condition in your head:
A **guard clause** handles each bad case first and leaves early. What remains is the happy path, flat and readable:
Each guard is the De Morgan negation of one nested condition. Every language with an early `return` supports this style.

steps.prompt: Each `return` leaves the function immediately. What is printed?
steps.explain: Because each guard returns, later checks can assume the earlier ones failed: by the `>= 50` line, `score` is known to be valid and under 90.

steps.prompt: Order the guards so `Ticket(10, false)` returns `"child"`, `Ticket(30, true)` returns `"member"` and `Ticket(30, false)` returns `"adult"`. Members of any age get the member price, so check that first.

steps.title: Flatten it
prompt: `CanVote` works but is nested three deep. Rewrite it with guard clauses: no `else`, and no `if` inside another `if`.
Rules: `age` under 18 gives `"too young"`, not registered gives `"not registered"`, already voted gives `"already voted"`, otherwise `"ok"`.
starter: string CanVote(int age, bool registered, bool voted)
solution: string CanVote(int age, bool registered, bool voted)
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("CanVote(17, true, false)", "too young", CanVote(17, true, false));
Dojo.Eq("CanVote(30, false, false)", "not registered", CanVote(30, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("CanVote(30, true, true)", "already voted", CanVote(30, true, true));
Dojo.Eq("CanVote(18, true, false)", "ok", CanVote(18, true, false));
hints: Negate each outer condition and return its failure message straight away.
`if (age < 18) return "too young";` is the first guard.

steps.title: Simplify the shipping rule
prompt: Write `bool FreeShipping(double total, bool isMember, bool isExpress)` as a single `return` of one clear expression.
Shipping is free when the order is **not** express **and** either the total is at least 50 or the customer is a member.
solution: bool FreeShipping(double total, bool isMember, bool isExpress)
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("60, not member, standard: free", true, FreeShipping(60, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("20, member, standard: free", true, FreeShipping(20, true, false));
Dojo.Eq("20, not member, standard: paid", false, FreeShipping(20, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("60, member, express: paid", false, FreeShipping(60, true, true));
Dojo.Eq("50 exactly counts", true, FreeShipping(50, false, false));

forbid.message: Does not compare booleans to true or false

hints: The "either" part needs parentheses, because `&&` binds tighter than `||`.

steps.title: What happens when you step there?
prompt: Every move in Delve asks one question: what happens if the hero steps onto `(x, y)`? Write **`static string MoveOutcome(string[] map, int x, int y, bool stairsOpen)`** with **guard clauses** (one `if ... return` per rule, no `else`, nothing nested), checking in this order:
1. a wall, or off the map: `"blocked"`

Reuse your earlier pieces instead of repeating them: **`IsWall(map, x, y)`** (De Morgan and short-circuits) and **`IsMonster(tile)`**, **`IsItem(tile)`** (Truth tables). The checks supply the reference versions of those three, so do not write them again here. Only read `map[y][x]` **after** the wall guard: off the map there is no tile to read.
starter: static string MoveOutcome(string[] map, int x, int y, bool stairsOpen)
solution: static string MoveOutcome(string[] map, int x, int y, bool stairsOpen)
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Try("MoveOutcome never crashes", () =>
Dojo.Eq("a wall is blocked", "blocked", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 0, 1, false));
Dojo.Eq("off the map is blocked", "blocked", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, -1, 1, false));
Dojo.Eq("far off the map is blocked", "blocked", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 3, 9, true));
Dojo.Eq("floor is a move", "move", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 1, 1, false));
Dojo.Eq("a goblin is a fight", "fight", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 2, 1, false));
Dojo.Eq("a mimic is a fight", "fight", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 1, 2, false));
Dojo.Eq("a dragon is a fight", "fight", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 3, 2, false));
Dojo.Eq("a chest is picked up", "pick up", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 3, 1, false));
Dojo.Eq("a potion is picked up", "pick up", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 2, 2, false));
Dojo.Eq("the key is picked up", "pick up", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 5, 1, false));
Dojo.Eq("closed stairs are locked", "locked", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 4, 1, false));
Dojo.Eq("open stairs: descend", "descend", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 4, 1, true));
Dojo.Eq("stairsOpen does not change a plain move", "move", MoveOutcome(dojoMap, 4, 2, true));
// src/Bounds.cs, as the reference solution wrote it
static bool IsOutsideMap(int x, int y, int width, int height)
return x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= width || y >= height;
static bool IsWall(string[] map, int x, int y)
return IsOutsideMap(x, y, map[0].Length, map.Length) || map[y][x] == '#';
// src/Rules.cs, as the reference solution wrote it
static bool CanOpenDoor(bool locked, bool hasKey, bool bossFloor, bool bossDefeated)
return (!locked || hasKey) && (!bossFloor || bossDefeated);
static bool IsMonster(char tile)
return tile == 'g' || tile == 'm' || tile == 'D';
static bool IsItem(char tile)
return tile == '$' || tile == 'k' || tile == '+';

forbid.message: Every function starts with `static` (Delve keeps its pieces in one static class)

hints: Start with the guard that keeps everything after it safe: `if (IsWall(map, x, y)) return "blocked";`
Then read the tile once into a box, `char tile = map[y][x];`, and give each remaining rule its own line.
Order matters for the stairs: the locked case has to be checked before the plain "descend".

build.title: Move rules
build.unlocks: Delve now has fights, treasure and locked stairs: every step asks your MoveOutcome what happens.
